summary: Verified L1-L5 Network Cap Cascade feature. All 9 backend tests pass. Cap formula min(8000, 800 + 16*L1 + 5*L2 + 3*L3 + 2*L4 + 1*L5) is correctly applied across /api/mining/rate-breakdown, /api/mining/status, /api/growth/network-stats, and /api/notifications/referrals/{uid}/level-breakdown. New fields cap_tier4_bonus / cap_tier5_bonus / cap_tier6_bonus / l3_count / l4_count / l5_count are present on all three primary endpoints. network_cap_formula string matches the locked formula. Discovered ONE inconsistency between mining.py and growth_economy.py — see backend_issues.minor.

minor.issue: mining.calculate_mining_rate counts direct_referrals via plain db.users.count_documents({'referred_by': uid}) — this misses L1 users whose referred_by stores the parent's referral_code instead of the parent's uid. growth_economy.get_growth_network_stats uses $or [{referred_by: uid}, {referred_by: referral_code}] so it returns the correct count. Net effect: when ANY L1 child stores the parent's referral_code, mining endpoint under-counts direct_referrals and under-reports cap_tier2_bonus (16*L1) and network_cap. Fix: change line 430 in /app/backend/routes/mining.py to use the same $or mixed-flavour query as growth_economy.py (line 540), OR simply use level_counts['l1'] from the BFS helper that is already being awaited in parallel.

action_items: Fix direct_referrals counting in /app/backend/routes/mining.py:calculate_mining_rate to use mixed uid/referral_code $or query (or reuse level_counts['l1'] from BFS) so mining endpoint matches growth_economy results when L1 children are linked via parent's referral_code.
critical_code_review_comments: Inconsistency: two separate sources of truth for L1 count — mining.py uses plain count_documents (uid only); growth_economy.py uses $or for mixed uid/referral_code. The new BFS helper (get_downline_level_counts) already returns correct L1 count via $in over uid+referral_code seed. Reuse it instead of calling count_documents separately.

Defensive default values (rate_info.get('cap_tier4_bonus', 0) etc.) in rate-breakdown response are good for backwards compatibility, but since these are guaranteed to be present in calculate_mining_rate's return dict, the .get() with default could be replaced with direct key access for clearer schema contract.

success_rate.frontend: N/A — backend only testing as requested

test_credentials: Used existing admin-test-123 (zero referrals base case). All other test users seeded directly via MongoDB with TEST-L1L5- prefix and cleaned up in fixture teardown.
seed_data_creation: Two seed chains used: (1) small chain — ROOT->2xL1->2xL2->1xL3->1xL4->1xL5 with mixed uid/referral_code referred_by, verified network_cap == 848; (2) max-cap chain — 500 L1 + 1000 L2 + 1000 L3 + 1000 L4 + 1000 L5 (raw_cap = 19800), verified clamped to 8000; (3) mixed-flavour chain — 1 L1 via uid + 1 L1 via referral_code, demonstrates inconsistency between mining and growth endpoints. All seed data deleted post-test (verified 7 real users intact, 0 TEST-L1L5- residue).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Feature implementation is correct and the cap math is sound. The single minor inconsistency in mining.calculate_mining_rate's direct_referrals counting should be addressed by the main agent — it does not break the 6-tier formula itself, only causes under-counting when L1 users store parent.referral_code instead of parent.uid. The test file at /app/backend/tests/test_l1l5_network_cap_cascade.py can be re-run after the fix; flip the assertion in TestMixedFlavourReferral.test_mining_rate_breakdown_mixed_flavour_bug from '== 1' to '== 2' to validate the fix. Fixture cleanup uses both per-uid delete AND a regex delete fallback for the max-cap chain.
rca of the issue: RCA for mining direct_referrals undercount: /app/backend/routes/mining.py line 429-433 awaits three coroutines in parallel — direct_referrals counts only via uid: db.users.count_documents({'referred_by': user_id}). The new BFS helper get_downline_level_counts (called in the same gather) correctly returns L1 count via $in([uid, referral_code]) at growth_economy.py line 324-327. The fix is to drop the separate count_documents call and use level_counts.get('l1', 0) — saves one query AND fixes the mismatch.
